item.title: Spain or Argentina, who will win the FIFA World Cup? Ex-player predictions
item.description:
Favourites and Foes: Ex-Players Weigh in on the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final

As the FIFA World Cup 2026 final draws near, the talk of the town is which team will emerge victorious: reigning European champions Spain, or defending champions Argentina. The predictions are flying in, and some of football’s most iconic players are weighing in with their opinions.

For many, the choice is clear: Spain are the team to beat. Former England striker Michael Owen has backed La Roja, calling them the “deserved” winners of the tournament. “Spain haven’t got the greatest individual players, I think France probably have,” Owen said, “but Spain as a team are everything England are not – they are brave, courageous with the ball.” Owen’s sentiments are echoed by Zlatan Ibrahimovic, who expects Spain to dominate the final. “Spain are going to do their thing,” Ibrahimovic said. “They’re going to play collectively… I believe Spain are going to dominate that game.”

item.title: Messi and Brady on 'prophetic' Lamine Yamal photos
item.description:
A Fateful Encounter: Messi and Brady Ponder the Prophetic Photos

Lionel Messi and Tom Brady are two of the most accomplished athletes of their respective generations, and yet, their paths converged in a moment that has been described as “very prophetic” by the NFL legend. The two sports icons gathered in New York, mere days before the World Cup final, to discuss a photograph that has taken on a life of its own – a snap from 2007 that captured Messi holding five-month-old Lamine Yamal, the current Spain captain.

item.title: World Cup 2026 latest: buildup to France v England third-place playoff and Spain v Argentina final
item.description:
A Final to Remember: The 2026 World Cup Showdown

As the sun sets on the 2026 World Cup, the stage is set for a thrilling final weekend. Tomorrow, Spain and Argentina will face off in New York/New Jersey, with the world watching as these two football giants clash in a battle for supremacy. But before the main event, the third-place playoff between France and England will take center stage in Miami, offering a tantalizing glimpse into the competitive spirit that has defined this tournament.

item.title: A-List: FIFA's top-4 make WC semis for first time
item.description:
The Unprecedented Quartet

The world’s top football nations are poised to etch their names in history as Argentina, Spain, France, and England made it past the quarterfinals of the World Cup, a feat no top-four ranked teams have ever achieved in the competition’s history. Argentina, the reigning champions, have been in scintillating form, with their impressive 3-0 win against Australia setting them up for a mouth-watering clash against the Netherlands in the semis. For France, the defending runners-up, a 2-1 victory over Poland secured their spot alongside England, who edged out Senegal 3-0 in the last eight. Meanwhile, Spain, who have been struggling for consistency throughout the tournament, edged out Croatia 3-1 in a high-intensity match.

item.title: Argentina set up England semi-final with extra-time victory over Switzerland
item.description:
Argentina’s Unyielding Spirit Propels Them Past Switzerland

In a pulsating extra-time encounter, Argentina scripted a thrilling 3-1 victory over 10-man Switzerland in Kansas City, setting up a highly anticipated World Cup semi-final showdown with England on Wednesday, 15 July. The match, marked by moments of brilliance and controversy, showcased the Argentine team’s unwavering determination and resilience.

As the match entered the high-stakes extra-time period, Argentina emerged from the shadows with a newfound sense of purpose, capitalizing on Switzerland’s numerical disadvantage to score twice and seal their semi-final berth. The Swiss, despite their valiant efforts, ultimately succumbed to the relentless pressure exerted by Argentina, whose players displayed a dogged refusal to yield. This dramatic turn of events sets the stage for a captivating encounter between Argentina and England, with the world watching in anticipation.
